messages:
anya: hey team! first-week onboarding hiccup. running the dev stack (colima + docker compose) and Sidekiq worker can't connect to Redis. container is Up but logs show `Could not connect to UNIX socket` from the app.

diego: welcome! do you have REDIS_URL pointing to a unix socket by accident? our example app supports both but defaults to socket if host is empty.

anya: hmm i was using `redis://%2Ftmp%2Fredis.sock` because local prod uses a socket. i switched to `redis://localhost:6379` and now app times out with `Connection refused`. redis container logs look fine though.

chris: if you run the worker inside a container, localhost is the container itself. compose service names are DNS hostnames (e.g., `redis`). try `redis://redis:6379`. also check if the redis service uses a unix socket file at `/tmp/redis.sock` mounted from host (bind-mount).

anya: i had a bind mount for `/tmp/redis.sock` to `./tmp/redis.sock` on host because i wanted the socket persisted for local testing. the redis container says the socket is created, but when the app tries to use it i get `Permission denied` from the socket path.

diego: sockets inherit host perms; on mac/colima the UID/GID mapping can block container access. three simple fixes: 1) use TCP in compose for dev (`host: redis, port: 6379`), 2) use a named volume for the socket directory instead of a host bind, 3) chown the host file to the redis uid (usually 100) so the container process can access it.

anya: tried `chown 100:100 ./tmp/redis.sock` but still permission errors. chris you mentioned colima mapping  any extra steps?

chris: with colima on arm you may need `colima stop` then `sudo chown 100:100 ./tmp -R` and restart colima so the VM re-reads the FS permissions. alternatively drop the socket mount and use the service hostname to avoid host/VM fs issues.

anya: removed the socket bind, set REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379, restarted compose and Sidekiq connects. redis is healthy and jobs run.

diego: nice. for docs we should mention: avoid host-mounted unix sockets for compose dev stacks on mac/colima; prefer TCP service hostnames or named volumes. include a short troubleshooting note: check service hostname, avoid `localhost` inside containers, and if you must bind sockets, ensure permissions match the container's uid and restart colima if needed.

infra-bot: Added a short note to the dev-setup guide: "Prefer TCP (service hostnames) over host unix sockets for compose dev stacks on mac/colima; if binding sockets, chown to container UID and restart Colima/Podman" https://go.redwood/dev-setup (:book:)

anya: thanks all! adding this to my onboarding doc and tagging @diego for a tiny quickstart update. :pray:
